newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT says paper results recovered in Q4.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT says paper results recovered in Q4.

text.p: Dutch paper group KNP BT said on Wednesday operating results at its paper-making unit KNP Leykam recovered slightly in the fourth quarter, helped by rising sales volumes and prices.
"During the last quarter, volumes resulted in good utilisation of machines and there was evidence of a slight rise in paper prices," KNP BT said in a statement.

The paper production activities posted a fourth quarter net profit of 26 million guilders, down from 84 million in the year-earlier period but up from a seven million guilder loss in the 1996 third quarter.
KNP BT earlier posted fourth quarter net profit from ordinary operations of 92 million guilders, down from 151 million in the year-earlier period.

Fourth quarter paper sales volumes amounted to 322,000 tonnes, down from 349,000 tonnes in the year-earlier period. But the comparison was skewed by the inclusion of KNP BT's paper mill in Bruck, Austria, in the 1995 figures, the firm said.
The mill was divested in late 1995. KNP BT said that it had been forced to fully write off the performance-related portion of the Bruck sale.
As a result the item 'Other financial results' had been propelled 15 million guilders into the red in the fourth quarter from a year-earlier eight million guilder loss.
Over the full year, these financial losses widened to 38 million guilders from five million.
KNP Leykam booked a full-year operating loss of five million guilders last year, after posting record operating profits of 375 million guilders in 1995.
Divestments accounted for around 60 million guilders of the decline, KNP BT said.
